evals.name: request-path
evals.prompt: Design a tool-independent diagram for Browser calling Orders through a load balancer. Orders uses a database and has a telemetry sidecar. A metrics collector receives background telemetry. Give a layout specification, not code.
evals.expected_output: Focus on the initiating request path; separate telemetry; embed the sidecar without implying the collector lives in the service; distinguish request direction from connections; consistent role colors and legend.

evals.name: crossings
evals.prompt: Review a proposed diagram showing tangled cross-region service calls. The crossings are intentional to show coupling. A direct diagonal also makes the layout cleaner. Should every crossing and diagonal be removed?
evals.expected_output: Allow informative or cleaner crossings while keeping endpoints traceable and junctions unambiguous; no orthogonal-only rule; avoid needless tangled streams.

evals.name: label-placement
evals.prompt: Fix a diagram where a boundary cuts through a subtitle and opaque arrow labels hide the middle of each arrow. Describe the changes.
evals.expected_output: Put each label fully inside or clearly outside its element; place arrow labels slightly above/below/beside the path, preferably near the source; keep the arrow visible rather than masking it.

evals.name: roles-and-states
evals.prompt: Specify a legend for infrastructure, load balancers/databases, and services. One service failed, one database is unhealthy, and a retry happens sometimes.
evals.expected_output: Consistent role palette and legend; red failed, amber/yellow unhealthy with explicit labels; preserve role identity; occasional retry dashed and slightly faded but readable; explain condition and avoid color-only meaning.

evals.name: concurrency-and-loops
evals.prompt: Simplify a comparison of a new connection per request versus connection reuse. Show TCP and TLS setup, requests, responses, closure, and concurrent requests. Do not check protocol details; identify assumptions.
evals.expected_output: Keep distinct phases and directions, accurate repeat scopes and one-time setup, preserve concurrency, stable comparison; flag unspecified protocol version/closure assumptions; do not invent serialization or delete meaningful steps.

evals.name: presentation
evals.prompt: A system diagram has twenty necessary components. It looks readable when zoomed to 200%, but will be projected on a conference slide. Improve its readability without changing its meaning.
evals.expected_output: Use overview/detail or a sequence of consistent views; retain necessary semantics; inspect actual presentation size; no arbitrary node cap or claim zoom fixes a projected slide.

evals.name: review-only
evals.prompt: Review a screenshot for diagram quality. It has a green database and blue services. The arrows and small labels are not discernible. Can you approve it? Do not change files.
evals.expected_output: Report supported findings; do not approve unreadable labels or infer hidden arrows/semantics; request inspectable output or name limits; keep review-only scope.

evals.name: non-trigger
evals.prompt: Fix a parser that mishandles an empty string. Do not change documentation, diagrams, or UI.
evals.expected_output: Do not apply diagram work or expand the requested scope.

evals.name: state-transitions
evals.prompt: Design a state diagram for Pending, Completed, and TimedOut. A response transitions Pending to Completed; a deadline transitions Pending to TimedOut. Once either transition wins, later events leave state unchanged. Give a layout specification without code.
evals.expected_output: Arrows mean guarded state transitions, not requests or network connections; preserve mutually exclusive terminal outcomes and no-op late events; keep concurrency/winner semantics explicit rather than relying on placement; use consistent state cues and legend if colors encode meaning; do not invent a shared lock implementation.
